- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30% for 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates prices; increase forecast lows by 10–25% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), producing exaggerated price surges; cap 30d forecast peaks at 1.5x recent 18d average.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak; if 30d forecast is >2.0x recent 18d average, apply downward correction to align with historical mean reversion pattern.
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model tends to overshoot mid-range; adjust forecast to center around 1.5–1.8x recent 18d mean.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a 5–10% downward bias to forecast to reflect lack of momentum.
